stem: A regional bank is starting its AWS adoption and expects to create about 25 accounts next quarter. It wants a prescriptive multi-account environment set up quickly, with preventive and detective guardrails and a standardized way to provision new accounts from an approved template. Which option meets these needs with the least custom work?

choices.text: AWS Control Tower, using its landing zone, controls and Account Factory
AWS Organizations with hand-written SCPs and a script that calls the CreateAccount API for each new account
AWS Service Catalog with a portfolio of CloudFormation products that teams launch into existing accounts
IAM Identity Center with permission sets that define what each team may do in its accounts

rationale: AWS Control Tower orchestrates AWS Organizations, AWS Service Catalog and IAM Identity Center to build a landing zone in under an hour, applies preventive, detective and proactive controls, and provides Account Factory as a configurable template for provisioning accounts. Organizations with hand-written SCPs and scripts can reach a similar result, but everything Control Tower sets up must then be built and maintained by hand. Service Catalog is one of the building blocks Control Tower uses; on its own it does not create the landing zone or its guardrails. IAM Identity Center manages workforce access to accounts; it does not provision accounts or apply governance controls.
